lines.text: JB Weld held so much weight that he ran out of weights and added a chunk of railroad iron.
It finally let go at 115 pounds and it snapped the brick before the glue.
Meanwhile Flex Glue held just 12 and a half pounds and Gorilla only 7 and a half which is less than a gallon of milk.
Because JB Weld is a two part epoxy that cures into hard plastic while the others stay rubbery so they can flex.
beats: ai:two part grey epoxy being mixed together on a metal plate macro

lines.text: On wood Loctite wins at 72 and a half pounds and Flex Glue ties JB Weld at 57 and a half.
Then he glues bolts into steel and JB Weld takes 204 inch pounds to break while every other glue lets go at zero.
So he pulls the head bolts out of an engine and lets JB Weld alone hold the head on.
And the engine blows the head loose which is the one job you should never give to any glue.
Because every firing stroke shoves the head up with thousands of pounds of force over and over.
beats: ai:a fiery combustion explosion inside an engine cylinder pushing up on the cylinder head

lines.text: So which glue would you trust?
